facts.name: transaction_authority

facts.name: counter_spike_oracle
facts.value: CounterSpike frozen oracle: initial state strictly (value=0, revision=0); from any (value=v, revision=r), accepting Increment(delta=1) transitions strictly to (v+1, r+1) and produces the unique domain Event CounterIncremented whose payload exactly contains the new value and new revision (command identity carried by the Controller envelope); any delta different from 1 returns typed INVALID_DELTA, leaves state completely unchanged, and produces no domain Event; expected-revision conflict handling is the Controller persistence layer's responsibility
facts.source: Reviewer direction (DRAFT review rounds 1 and 2, REWORK)

facts.name: port_direction
facts.value: the persistence port is private to the Controller; the accepted ControllerCommandPort.submit(command: ControllerCommand) -> CommandReceipt signature is the external Interface and the only Interface the Stage Executor may call; the Stage Executor and graph code must not import the private persistence port, persistence Adapters, SQLAlchemy, or database files
facts.source: Accepted system-and-module-design.md plus Codex corrective attempt after two Executor reworks

facts.name: typed_failure_boundary
facts.value: the existing CommandReceipt status/error model carries safe translated Controller failures: INVALID_DELTA projects to REJECTED/VALIDATION_ERROR with fixed message invalid delta; conflicts project to CONFLICT/CONFLICT with fixed safe messages; SQLITE_FULL and persistence unavailability project to a non-durable REJECTED/INTERNAL_ERROR receipt with fixed message persistence unavailable and retryable=true; backup and migration helpers return bounded non-serialized typed results; raw sqlite3, SQLAlchemy, or driver exceptions never cross Interfaces; no committed Schema or accepted Interface changes
facts.source: coding-and-test-standard.md, command-receipt.schema.json, accepted system-and-module-design.md, and Codex corrective attempt

facts.name: crash_vs_transaction_evidence
facts.value: AC-03 injects exceptions before and after each logical write inside the transaction for rollback evidence; AC-05 crashes a real subprocess only at the pre-commit and post-commit durable boundaries and restarts a fresh process from the same database and WAL; exception injection is never presented as crash evidence

facts.name: backup_policy
facts.value: the backup API and policy reject the raw-copy path before any I/O; a guard or mock proves the implementation only ever calls sqlite3.Connection.backup(); no assertion that a raw copy necessarily corrupts is permitted; the backup helper returns bounded typed results

facts.name: sqlite_version_predicate
facts.value: exact predicate: at least 3.51.3, or at least 3.50.7 and below 3.51.0, or at least 3.44.6 and below 3.45.0; committed accept vectors (3.51.3, 3.51.4, 3.50.7, 3.50.8, 3.44.6, 3.44.7) and reject vectors (3.51.2, 3.51.0, 3.50.6, 3.44.5, 3.43.0); a failing linked library on either platform stops the Slice with a Contract Change Request before claiming any spike persistence conclusion
facts.source: Research note and reviewer direction (DRAFT review round 1, REWORK)

facts.name: driver_transaction_mode
facts.value: the spike selects and tests one explicit SQLite driver transaction mode (for example SQLAlchemy connect_args autocommit=False or an explicit BEGIN event hook); the legacy sqlite3 default transaction control is never relied on; Alembic begin_transaction is a logical migration transaction and whole-migration rollback atomicity is never promised; an injected migration failure recovers through the verified backup and recovery path

facts.name: workload_envelope
facts.value: fixed reproducible envelope: 1,000 accepted commands, 4 producers, one writer, queue capacity 32, command and event payloads each no larger than 1 KiB, p95 acknowledged latency no greater than 2 seconds, busy count equal to 0, WAL high-water no greater than 16 MiB, and checkpoint, online backup, and fresh-process recovery each no greater than 5 seconds; the report records a fixed redacted runner profile (OS family, architecture, CI runner label, Python version, and sqlite3.sqlite_version) plus selected PRAGMAs and queue high-water; hostname, username, absolute paths, environment variable values, tokens, raw exception text, and database content are forbidden, proved by a redaction assertion with injected fake sensitive values; a deterministic SQLITE_FULL injection returns the specified non-durable REJECTED/INTERNAL_ERROR receipt, writes no durable receipt record or partial records, and is restart-safe; an exceeded limit triggers the replacement-ADR path (Phase risk R-03)
facts.source: Observability-recovery-and-runbooks.md, PHASE.md R-03, reviewer direction, and Codex corrective attempt

facts.name: ccr_sqlite_version_gate_resolution
facts.value: revision 6 attempt 1 stopped BLOCKED_CONTRACT because the managed Windows runtime (CPython 3.12.10) linked SQLite 3.49.1, failing the exact WAL-reset predicate (>=3.51.3 OR (>=3.50.7 AND <3.51.0) OR (>=3.44.6 AND <3.45.0)); human resolution 2026-08-08 (revision 7): predicate unchanged and still an independent per-platform gate; managed interpreter pinned to uv-managed CPython 3.12.13 (Astral build) via .python-version and python-quality.yml (setup-uv python-version 3.12.13, job env UV_MANAGED_PYTHON=1); CI responsibility split — documentation-contracts.yml stays at 3.12, check_documentation.py carries split constants, tests/test_quality_workflow.py gains the managed-Python negative test; permitted paths extended to .python-version, .github/workflows/python-quality.yml, scripts/check_documentation.py, tests/test_quality_workflow.py
facts.source: human CCR decision 2026-08-08; SLICE.md Revision 7 section; compatibility-targets.md revision-7 section

facts.name: previous_review_findings
facts.value: DRAFT review round 1 returned REWORK (all addressed in revision 2): manifest missing dependency and CI authority inputs; complete offline verification not contractually executable; Alembic had no acceptance criterion; workload and recovery thresholds not reproducible and SQLITE_FULL injection missing; Stage Executor and private persistence port boundary contradictory; raw WAL copy negative case indeterminate; domain oracle too abstract; SQLite safety version rule imprecise; transaction fault and real process crash conflated. DRAFT review round 2 returned REWORK (all addressed in revision 3): ControllerCommandPort missing a safe typed failure boundary allowing raw driver exceptions, SQL, paths, or database content to leak to callers; runner identity lacking a redaction rule; CounterSpike success semantics not a unique oracle. Final READY review found that SubmitResult silently changed the accepted ControllerCommand -> CommandReceipt Interface and required a new external error family despite frozen schemas. Per the two-rework ownership rule, Codex performed one bounded corrective attempt in revisions 4 and 5: it restored the accepted signature, mapped failures through existing CommandReceipt status/error values, and made the architecture-required private COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT classification mandatory while retaining the public CONFLICT/CONFLICT receipt mapping; it changed no Schema, dependency, scope, authority, or product behavior.
facts.source: DRAFT review rounds 1 and 2, final READY review, and Codex corrective attempt
